title: Lake Van temple basalt brought from 350 miles away
place_text: Lake Van region sites (Ayanis, Kef Kalesi, Çavuştepe), Turkey

tellings.quote: some of the balt that they used in this this construction is considered to possibly come from 350 miles away

plain: Some of the basalt, a dark volcanic stone, used to build the ancient temples and fortresses around Lake Van in eastern Turkey, at sites such as Ayanis, Kef Kalesi and Çavuştepe, may have been hauled from as far as 350 miles away. A researcher named Matt LaCroix says this without naming a source, as a sign that the builders were capable of more than is usually assumed.
